bio.en: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar are the leading voices on AI evals—Hamel a veteran ML engineer (formerly at GitHub and Airbnb) and Shreya a PhD researcher at Stanford—who teach the definitive online course that has trained over 2,000 PMs and engineers across 500 companies, including the teams at OpenAI and Anthropic.
bio.zh: Hamel Husain 与 Shreya Shankar 是 AI 评估（evals）领域最具代表性的声音——Hamel 是一位资深机器学习工程师（曾任职于 GitHub 和 Airbnb），Shreya 是斯坦福的博士研究员——他们开设的权威在线课程已培训超过 2000 名 PM 与工程师、覆盖 500 家公司，其中包括 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的团队。

summary.en: Hamel and Shreya make the case that building evals is the highest-ROI activity for any AI product team, and that you only need to do the process once to build on it—not perfectly, but actionably. They dismantle common misconceptions (no, the AI can't just eval itself; no, you don't need a committee—appoint one trusted 'benevolent dictator' with domain expertise). The episode is a show-and-tell primer: walking through how to build an effective eval, the first steps to start, and battle-tested best practices, leaving even non-technical listeners excited to write their own.

(00:12:36): So let's go through the very beginning stage, what we call error analysis, which is, let's look at the data of their application and first start with what's going wrong. So I'm going to jump to that next, and I'm going to open an observability tool. And you can use whatever you want here. I just happen to have this data loaded in a tool called Braintrust, but you can load it in anything. We don't have a favorite tool or anything in the blog post that we wrote with you. We had the same example but in Phoenix Arize, and I think Aman, on your blog post, used Phoenix Arize as well. And there's also LangSmith. So these are kind of like different tools that you can use. (00:13:29): So what you see here on the screen, this is logs from the application, and let me just show you how it looks. So it's called a trace, and it's just the engineering term for logs of a sequence of events. The concept of a trace has been around for a really long time, but it's especially really important when it comes to AI applications. (00:14:12): And so we have all the different components and pieces and information that the AI needs to do its job, and we are logged all of it and we're looking at a view of that. And so you see here a system prompt. The system prompt says, "You are an AI assistant working as a leasing team member at Retreat at Acme Apartments." turns.zh: 好，我先稍微交代一下背景。呼应 Shreya 所说的，非常重要的一点是，不能只把评测当成测试。很多人会掉进一个常见陷阱：他们直接跳到测试上，心想："让我写些测试。"但通常这不是你最该先做的。你应该先做某种数据分析，借此确定到底该测试什么；这和软件工程有些不同，因为在软件工程里，你对系统如何工作有更多预期。LLM 的覆盖面大得多，也高度随机，因此这里的做法不一样。(00:10:47)：今天我要展示的例子是一个房地产案例，但与刚才的类型不同，来自一家名为 Nurture Boss 的公司。我可以分享屏幕，展示他们的网站，帮助你稍微理解这个用例。我曾与这家公司合作过，Nurture Boss 是面向公寓物业管理人员的 AI 助手，可协助处理潜在客户咨询、客户服务、预约等各种事务。作为物业经理可能会处理的各类运营工作，它都能提供帮助。它是很好的例子，因为它具备现代 AI 应用的许多复杂性。(00:11:40)：用户可以通过聊天、短信、语音等许多不同渠道与 AI 互动；此外还有工具调用，包括大量用于预约、查询可用信息等的工具调用。它也有 RAG 检索，用于获取客户、房源等相关信息。作为 AI 应用来说，它相当完整。他们非常慷慨地允许我把他们的数据作为教学案例。我们已将其匿名化；今天我要带大家走的是：我们该如何开始为 Nurture Boss 构建评测？又为什么要这样做？(00:12:36)：让我们从最开始的阶段讲起，我们称之为错误分析，也就是先查看应用数据，找出哪里出了问题。接下来我会打开一个可观测性工具。你可以使用任何工具；我只是恰好把数据加载到了一个叫 Braintrust 的工具里。我们没有偏爱的工具。在我们和你一起写的博客文章中，我们用同一个例子展示了 Phoenix Arize；我想 Aman 在你的博客文章里也使用了 Phoenix Arize。另外还有 LangSmith，这些都是可以使用的不同工具。(00:13:29)：你现在屏幕上看到的是应用日志，我先让你看看它是什么样子。让我全屏一下：这是一个客户与 Nurture Boss 应用进行的特定交互，其中详细记录了发生的一切。它被称为 trace，也就是一连串事件日志的工程术语。trace 这个概念已经存在很久，但对 AI 应用尤其重要。(00:14:12)：我们记录了 AI 完成工作所需的各种组件、信息和环节，现在看到的就是这些记录。你会看到一个系统提示词，它写着："你是一名 AI 助手，作为 Retreat at Acme Apartments 租赁团队的一员工作。"记得我说过数据已经匿名化了，所以才会用 Acme Apartments 这个名字。"你的主要职责是回复现有住户和潜在住户的短信。你的目标是提供准确、有帮助的信息。"诸如此类。后面还有很多关于我们希望这个系统如何表现的详细指南。

turns.en: It is. Yes, it is.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah. Yeah, it's really cool. And you see all of these different sort of features that are different use cases, so things about tour scheduling, handling applications, guidance on how to talk to different personas, so on and so forth. And you can see the user just kind of jumps in here and asks, "Okay, do you have a one-bedroom with study available? I saw it on virtual tours." And then you can see that the LLM calls some tools. It calls this get individual's information tool, and it pulls back that person's information. And then it gets the community's availability. So it's querying a database with the availability for that apartment complex. (00:16:01): And then finally, the AI responds, "Hey, we have several one-bedroom apartments available, but none specifically listed with a study. Here are a few options." (00:16:12): And then it says, "Can you let me know when one with a study is available?" (00:16:16): And then it says, "I currently don't have specific information on the availability of a one-bedroom apartment." (00:16:23): User says, "Thank you." (00:16:25): And the AI says, "You're welcome. If you have any more questions, feel free to reach out." Now, this is an example of a trace, and we're looking at one specific data point. And so one thing that's really important to do when you're doing data analysis of your LLM application is to look at data. Now, you might wonder, "There's a lot of these logs. It's kind of messy. There's a lot of things going on here. How in the hell are you supposed to look at this data? Do you want to just drown in this data? How do you even analyze this data?" (00:17:07): So it turns out there is a way to do it that is completely manageable, and it's not something that we invented. It's been around in machine learning and data science for a really long time, and it's called error analysis. And what you do is, the first step in conquering data like this is just to write notes. Okay? So you got to put your product hat on, which is why we're talking to you, because product people have to be in the room and they have to be involved in sort of doing this. Usually a developer is not suited to do this, especially if it's not a coding application.
turns.zh: 是的，确实很酷。你能看到各种不同功能和用例，例如看房预约、处理申请、如何与不同用户角色沟通的指引，等等。用户进来问："好的，你们有带书房的一居室吗？我在虚拟看房里看到了。"随后你可以看到 LLM 调用了几个工具：它调用了获取个人信息的工具，拉取这个人的信息；然后又查询社区房源可用情况，也就是查询这个公寓社区的房源数据库。(00:16:01)：最后，AI 回复说："你好，我们有几套一居室公寓可供选择，但没有明确标注带书房的。这里有几个选项。"(00:16:12)：随后用户说："如果有带书房的房源，你能告诉我吗？"(00:16:16)：AI 说："我目前没有关于带书房一居室公寓可用情况的具体信息。"(00:16:23)：用户说："谢谢。"(00:16:25)：AI 说："不客气。如果你还有其他问题，随时联系。"这就是一个 trace 的例子，我们正在查看一个具体数据点。对 LLM 应用做数据分析时，非常重要的一件事就是直接看数据。你可能会想："这里有很多日志，乱糟糟的，发生了很多事。到底该怎么看这些数据？难道要淹没在这些数据里吗？又该如何分析？"(00:17:07)：其实有一种完全可控的方法，而且不是我们发明的。它在机器学习和数据科学领域已经存在很久，叫作错误分析。面对这类数据，第一步就是写下笔记。明白吗？你得戴上产品帽，这也是我们正在和你聊这个话题的原因：产品人员必须在场，并参与这类工作。通常，开发者并不适合独自做这件事，特别是在不是编程类应用的时候。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And just to mirror back, why I think you're saying that is because this is the user experience of your product. People talking to this agent is the entire product essentially, and so it makes sense for the product person to be super involved in this.
turns.zh: 我来复述一下：我理解你之所以这么说，是因为这就是你产品的用户体验。用户与这个智能体交谈，本质上就是整个产品，所以产品人员深度参与其中是很合理的。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah. So let's reflect on this conversation. Okay, a user asked about availability. The AI said, "Oh, we don't really have that. Have a nice day." Now, for a product that is helping you with lead management, is that good? Do you feel like this is the way we want it to go?
turns.zh: 是啊。所以让我们回顾一下这次对话。好的，有位用户询问了产品的可用性。人工智能回答说：“哦，我们这里确实没有这个功能。祝你今天愉快。” 现在，针对一款帮助你进行潜在客户管理的产品，这样的回应合适吗？你觉得这正是我们希望的服务体验吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Not ideal.
turns.zh: 不是很理想。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yes, not ideal, and I'm glad you said that. A lot of people would say, "Oh, it's great. The AI did the right thing. It looked, it said, 'We didn't have available,' and it's not available." But with your product hat on, you know that's not correct. And so what you would do is you would just write a quick note here. You would say, "Okay." You might pop in here, and you can write a note. So every observability application has ability to write notes, and you wouldn't try to figure out if something is wrong. In this case, it's kind of not doing the right thing, but you just write a quick note, "Should have handed off to a human."
turns.zh: 是的，这确实不理想，我很高兴你能指出这一点。很多人的反应可能是："哦，太棒了。AI做得很正确。它查看了数据，提示'我们没有空房'，然后就认定确实没有空房了。"但从产品角度来看，你知道这种处理方式并不正确。所以你只需在这里快速记录一下情况。比如你可以写道："好的，我需要处理这个问题。"你可以在系统中添加备注，每个可观测性应用都具备添加备注的功能，这样你就不必去纠结是否存在什么问题。这种情况下，AI的处理方式确实不符合预期，但你只需简单记录一下："应该把这个任务交给人工处理的。"

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And as we watch this happening, it's like you mention this and you'll explain more. You're doing this, this feels very manual and unscalable, but as you said, this is just one step of the process and there's a system to this. That was just the first one.
turns.zh: 看着这一切发生，感觉你提到了这件事，但还需要进一步解释。你现在做的事情看起来非常依赖人工操作，缺乏可扩展性。但正如你所说，这只是整个流程中的一步，背后肯定有系统的支撑。这只是第一步。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah, and you don't have to do it for all of your data. You sample your data and just take a look, and it's surprising how much you learn when you do this. Everyone that does this immediately gets addicted to it and they say, "This is the greatest thing that you can do when you're building an AI application." You just learn a lot and you're like, "Hmm, this is not how I want it to work. Okay." And so that's just an example. (00:19:58): So you write this note, and then we can go on to the next trace. So this is the next trace. I just pushed a hot key on my keyboard. Let me go back to looking at it.
turns.zh: 是啊，你不必对所有数据都这样做。你只需抽样部分数据进行分析，结果会让你惊讶地发现能从中获取大量信息。每个尝试过的人都会立刻沉迷其中，并感叹："这真是开发人工智能应用时最棒的做法。"你能学到很多东西，然后会想："嗯，我不希望它这样运行。好吧。"这只是个例子。（00:19:58）你写下这段注释后，我们就可以继续下一个跟踪了。这是下一个跟踪。我刚在键盘上按了一个快捷键。让我再回来看看。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And these tools make it easy to go through a bunch and add these notes quickly.
turns.zh: 这些工具能让用户轻松浏览大量内容，并快速添加注释。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yes. And so this is another one. Similar system prompt. We don't need to go through all of it again. We'll just jump right into the user question. "Okay, I've been texting you all day." Isn't that funny? And the user says, "Please." Okay, yeah, this one is just like an error in the application where this is a text message application, sorry, the channel through which the customer is communicating is through text message, and you're just getting really garbled. And you can see here that it kind of doesn't make sense. The words are being cut off like, "In the meantime," and then the system doesn't know how to respond, because you know how people text message, they write short phrases. They split their sentence across four or five different turns. So in this case-
turns.zh: 是的。这又是一个类似的系统提示。我们不需要再把整个过程讲一遍，直接进入用户的问题部分。"好的，我一整天都在给你发短信。"这不是很有趣吗？用户说："拜托。"好的，是的，这个问题其实是应用程序中的一个错误。这是一个短信应用程序，抱歉，客户是通过短信进行沟通的，但你收到的消息却语无伦次。你可以看到这里内容有些不通顺，比如"与此同时"之类的词被截断了，而系统也不知道该如何回应，因为你知道人们发短信时通常会用简短的句子，把一句话分成四五个短语。所以在这种情况下——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, so what do you do with something like that?
turns.zh: 是啊，那遇到这种情况该怎么处理呢？

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah, so this is a different kind of error.
turns.zh: 是啊，所以这是一种不同类型的错误。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Mm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: This is more of, "Hey, we're not handling this interaction correctly. This is more of a technical problem," rather than, "Hey, the AI is not doing exactly what we want." So we would write that down too.
turns.zh: 这更像是在说，"嘿，我们处理这次互动的方式不对。这更多是一个技术问题"，而不是"嘿，人工智能没有完全按照我们的要求去做。"所以我们也会把这部分记录下来。

turns.speaker: Lenny

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah, you might not know this is happening, right? And so you would just say, "Okay." You would write a note like, "Oh, conversation flow is janky because of text message."
turns.zh: 是啊，你可能都不知道这事儿正在发生，对吧？所以你只能说，“好吧。”然后写个备注，比如“哎，聊天进度卡得这么严重，肯定是短信的问题。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I like that, I like that you're using the word janky. It shows you just how informal this can be at this stage.
turns.zh: 嗯，我喜欢这样，我喜欢你用“不靠谱”这个词。这显示出在现阶段交流可以有多随意、多口语化。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah, it's supposed to be chill. Just don't overthink it. And there's a way to do this. So the question always comes up, how do you do this? Do you try to find all the different problems in this trace? What do you write a note about? And the answer is, just write down the first thing that you see that's wrong, the most upstream error. Don't worry about all the errors, just capture the first thing that you see that's wrong, and stop, and move on. And you can get really good at this. The first two or three can be very painful, but you can do a bunch of them really fast. (00:22:38): So here's another one, and let's skip the system prompt again. And the user asks, "Hey, I'm looking for a two- to three-bedroom with either one or two baths. Do you provide virtual tours?" (00:22:51): And a bunch of tools are called and it says, "Hi Sarah. Currently, we have three-bedroom, two-and-a-half-bathroom apartment available for $2,175. Unfortunately, we don't have any two-bedroom options at the moment. We do offer virtual tours. You can schedule a tour," blah, blah. It just so happens that there is no virtual tour, right?
turns.zh: 是啊，本来就应该保持轻松。别想太多。做这件事有诀窍的。所以总有人问，具体该怎么做？要逐一找出日志中的所有问题吗？该记录哪些内容？答案是：先记下你第一眼看到的错误，最根本的那个。别纠结于所有错误，抓住最明显的那个就停下，继续往下看。这样练多了自然熟练。前两三次可能会很痛苦，但之后就能快速应对了。（00:22:38）再看另一个例子，还是跳过系统提示。用户问：“嘿，我想找一套两到三居室的房子，带一到两个卫生间。你们提供虚拟看房服务吗？” （00:22:51）系统调用了多个工具，回复道：“嗨，莎拉。目前我们有三居室、两卫半的公寓在出租，价格2175美元。很遗憾，目前没有两居室房源。我们确实提供虚拟看房服务，你可以预约看房”之类的。但关键是现在根本没有虚拟看房功能，对吧？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Mm-hmm. Nice.
turns.zh: 嗯，不错啊。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: So it is hallucinating something that doesn't exist. Then you kind of have to bring your context as an engineer, or even product content, and say, "Hey, this is kind of weird. We shouldn't be telling a person about virtual tour when it's not offered." (00:23:32): So you would say, "Okay, offered virtual tour," and you just write the note. So you can see there's a diversity of different kinds of errors that we're seeing, and we're actually learning a lot about your application in a very short amount of time.
turns.zh: 也就是说，用户看到了一些根本不存在的东西。这时候，作为工程师或产品负责人，我们需要结合上下文，指出：“嘿，这有点奇怪。我们不应该向用户推荐虚拟导览服务，如果这项功能根本不存在的话。” （00:23:32）然后，你可以回复：“好的，虚拟导览功能已启用。”并记录下相关信息。由此可见，我们发现了各种各样的错误类型，而且在极短的时间内就对你的应用有了深入的了解。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: One common question that we get from people at this stage is, "Okay, I understand what's going on. Can I ask an LLM to do this process for me?"
turns.zh: 现阶段，我们经常收到人们提出的一个常见问题是：“好的，我明白整个流程了。那我能请LLM（法律硕士）来帮我完成这个步骤吗？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Mm, great question.
turns.zh: 嗯，问得好。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: And I loved Hamel's most recent example because what we usually find when we try to ask an LLM to do this error analysis is it just says the trace looks good because it doesn't have the context needed to understand whether something might be bad product smell or not. For example, the hallucination about scheduling the tour, right? I can guarantee you, I would bet money on this, if I put that into chat GPT and asked, "Is there an error?" it would say, "No, did a great job." (00:24:34): But Hamel had the context of knowing, "Oh, we don't actually have this virtual tour functionality," right? So I think, in these cases, it's so important to make sure you are manually doing this yourself. And we can talk a little bit more about when to use LLMs in the process later, but number one pitfall right here is people are like, "Let me automate this with an LLM."

You might have to go through it again if you need more data, and there's a lot of details to this on how to do this correctly. You want to split your data and do all these things, so that you're not cheating, but I just want to show you the concept. Basically, what you can do is measure the agreement. Now, one thing you should know, as a product manager, is a lot of people go straight to this agreement. They say, "Okay, my judge agrees with the human some percentage of the time." (00:58:41): Now that sounds appealing, but it's a very dangerous metric to use, because a lot of times, errors, they only happen on the long tail and they don't happen as frequently, so if you only have the error 10% of the time, then you can easily have 90% agreement by just having a judge say it passes all the time. Does that make sense? 90% agreement look good on paper, but it might be misleading.
turns.zh: 是啊，是啊，我们已经做过了。我们已经手动检查过了。没必要再重复一遍，因为我们有来自轴向编码的作弊代码，之前已经处理过了。如果你需要更多数据，可能还得再检查一遍，而且正确操作有很多细节要掌握。你需要拆分数据并完成所有这些步骤，这样才不算作弊，但我只是想向你展示这个概念。基本上，你可以衡量一致性。作为产品经理，你应该知道很多人直接使用这个一致性指标。他们会说：“好吧，我的评分员和人工评分在一定比例的情况下达成一致。”（00:58:41）这听起来挺吸引人的，但这是一个非常危险的衡量标准，因为很多错误只出现在长尾部分，出现频率很低。所以如果你只有10%的错误率，那么只要让评分员每次都说通过，你就能轻松达到90%的准确率。这下明白了吧？90%的准确率看起来很棒，但可能存在误导。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's rare, it's a rare error. Yeah.
turns.zh: 这太罕见了，这是一个罕见的错误。是啊。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: As a product manager or someone, even if you're not doing this calculation yourself, if someone ever reports to you agreement, you should immediately ask, "Okay, tell me more." You need to look into it. They give you more intuition, here is like a matrix of this specific judge in the Google sheet, and this is, again, a pivot table, just keeping it dumb and simple. "Okay, on the rows I have, what did the human think? What did I think? Did it have an error, true or false? Then did my judge have an error, true or false?"
turns.zh: 作为产品经理或其他相关人士，即便你自己不参与这项数据分析，但如果有人向你汇报达成一致的结果，你也应该立即追问：“好的，请详细说说。”你需要深入探究背后的原因。这里以Google表格中的特定评分矩阵为例，再次用最直观的表格形式呈现（保持简洁易懂）：“好的，我这里的行数据里，人类评分员是怎么评价的？我自己是怎么评分的？是否存在评分错误？结果是正确还是错误？然后我的评分员是否也犯了类似的错误？正确还是错误？”

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: The intuition here is exactly what Hamel said, where you need to look at each type of error. When the human said false, but the judge said true, or vice versa, so those non-green diagonals here, and if they're too large, then go iterate on your prompt, make it more clear to the LLM judge, so that you can reduce that misalignment. You want to get to a point where most... You're going to have some misalignment, that's okay. We talk about in our course, also how to code correct that misalignment, but in this stage, if you're a product manager and the person who's building the LLM judge eval has not done this, they're saying like, "It agrees 75% of the time, we're good." They don't have this matrix and they haven't iterated to make sure that these two types of errors have gone down to zero, then it's a bad smell. Go and ask them to go fix that.
turns.zh: 这种直觉正是哈梅尔所说的，你需要逐一分析每种类型的错误。例如，当人类评分者判定某个答案错误，而评分引擎却给出正确判定，或者反之亦然——即这些非绿色的对角线——如果误差过大，那么你就需要迭代优化你的提示语，使其更清晰易懂，让LLM评分引擎更容易理解，从而减少这种不一致性。你的目标是让大多数情况下……不一致是难免的，但我们在课程中也讲解了如何通过代码修复这种不一致性。但在现阶段，如果你是一位产品经理，而负责开发LLM评分引擎的团队却没有做到这些——比如他们只说"准确率达到75%，没问题"，却没有构建这样的矩阵表，也没有通过迭代确保这两类错误率降至零——这就是一个警示信号。你需要督促他们去改进。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. That's a really good tip, what to look for when someone's doing this wrong.
turns.zh: 太棒了。这真是个很棒的建议，告诉我们在别人做错的时候该注意什么。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Actually, can you take us back to the LLM as judge prompt? I just want to highlight something really interesting here. I've had some guests on the podcast recently who've been saying, "Evals are the new PRDs," and if you look at this, this is exactly what this is. Product managers, product teams, here's what the product should be, here's all the requirements, here's the how it should work. They built a thing and then they test it. Manually, often. What's cool about this is this is exactly that same thing, and it's running constantly. It's telling you, "Here's how this agent should respond," and it's very specific ways. "If it's this, this, this, do that. If it's this, this, that, do that." It's exactly what I've been hearing again and again, you could see right here. This is the purest sense of what a product requirements document should be, is this eval judge that's telling you exactly what it should be, and it's automatic and running constantly.
turns.zh: 实际上，能否请您把我们带回到LLM作为评分器的示例中？我只是想强调一个非常有趣的点。最近我邀请了几位嘉宾参加播客，他们都说"评估文档就是新的产品需求文档"。仔细看看这里的情况，这正是其本质所在。产品经理和产品团队会制定产品规范，列出所有需求，说明产品应如何运作。他们开发出产品后，通常会手动测试。而这里的妙处在于，它做着同样的事情——而且是持续运行的。它会告诉你"这个智能体应该如何回应"，并给出非常具体的指令。比如"如果是这种情况，就这样做；如果是那种情况，就那样做"。这正是我反复听到的观点，从这里就能看出来。这种评估评分器能准确告知产品应达到的标准，完全自动化且持续运行，这正是产品需求文档应有的终极形态。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. It's derived from our own data, so of course, it's a product manager's expectations. What I find that a lot of people miss is they just put in what their expectations are before looking at their data, but as we look at our data, we uncover more expectations that we couldn't have dreamed up in the first place, and that ends up going into this prompt.
turns.zh: 是的，当然可以。这是基于我们自身的数据得出的，所以这无疑是产品经理的预期。我发现很多人会先设定自己的预期，然后才去查看数据。但当我们真正分析数据时，往往会发现更多超出最初想象的需求，而这些需求最终都会被纳入产品设计的考量中。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is interesting. Your advice is not skip straight to evals and LLM as judge prompts before you build the product, still write traditional one-pagers PRDs to tell your team what we're doing, why we're doing it, what success looks like. But then at the end, you could probably pull from that and even improve that original PRD if you're evolving the product using this process.
turns.zh: 很有意思。你的建议是，在开发产品之前，先不要直接跳到评估和LLM阶段（即法官提示阶段），而是先写传统的单页PRD文档，向团队说明我们要做什么、为什么要做、成功的标准是什么。然后，当产品在迭代过程中，再以此为基础进行优化，甚至进一步完善最初的PRD文档。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I would go even further to say you're going to improve... It's going to change. You're never going to know what the failure modes are going to be upfront, and you're always going to uncover new vibes that you think that your product should have. You don't really know what you want until you see it with these LLMs, so you got to be flexible, have to look at your data, have to... PRDs are a great abstraction for thinking about this. It's not the end all, be all. It's going to change.
turns.zh: 我甚至可以进一步说，你的改进空间是无穷的……一切都将与时俱进。你永远无法预知产品会出现哪些故障模式，总会发现一些你原本以为产品应该具备的新特性。在使用这些大语言模型之前，你根本不知道自己真正想要什么，所以必须保持灵活，善于分析数据……产品需求文档（PRD）是思考这些问题的绝佳抽象工具，但它并非万能灵药。一切都在不断变化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that, and Hamel's pulling up some cool research report. What's this about?
turns.zh: 我太喜欢这个了，哈梅尔又找到了份很棒的研究报告。这报告讲的是什么？

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: This is one of the coolest research reports you can possibly read if you want to know about evals. It was authored by someone named Shreya Shankar.
turns.zh: 如果你想了解评估相关内容，那么这份研究报告绝对是你能读到的最酷的资料之一。它由名为Shreya Shankar的研究者撰写。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Oh, my God.
turns.zh: 哦，我的天哪。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: And her collaborators. It's called "Who Validates the Validated?"
turns.zh: 以及她的合作伙伴们。这部作品名为《谁来验证那些被验证的人？》

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's the best name for a researcher.
turns.zh: 真是个适合研究者的绝佳名字啊。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Thank you, thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢，谢谢。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: I should let Shreya talk about this. I think one of the most important things to pay attention in this paper are the criteria drift, and what she found.
turns.zh: 我应该让施瑞亚来谈谈这个问题。我认为这篇论文中最值得关注的点之一是标准偏差问题，以及她在研究中发现的相关结论。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: We did this super fun study when we were doing user studies with people who were trying to write LLM judges or just validate their own LLM outputs. I think this was before evals was extremely popular, I feel like, on the internet. We did this project late 2023 was when we started it. But then the thing that really was burning in my mind as a researcher is like, "Why is this problem so hard? We've been having machine learning and AI for so long, it's not new, but suddenly, this time around, everything is really difficult." We just did this user study with a bunch of developers and we realized, "Okay, what's new here is that you can't figure out your rubrics upfront. People's opinions of good and bad change as they review more outputs, they think of failure modes only after seeing 10 outputs they would never have dreamed of in the first place," and these are experts. These are people who have built many LLM pipelines and now agents before, and you can't ever dream up everything in the first place. I think that's so key in today's world of AI development.
turns.zh: 当时我们在做用户研究，研究对象是那些尝试编写LLM评分标准或验证自己LLM输出的人。那时候，LLM评估（evals）在互联网上还没像现在这么火爆。我记得这个项目始于2023年末。但作为研究者，当时最困惑的问题是：“为什么这个问题如此难解？机器学习和AI技术早已存在，并非新鲜事物，但为何这次却困难重重？”我们对一群开发者进行了用户研究，发现问题关键在于：无法预先制定评分标准。用户在评审大量输出样例后，对“好坏”的标准会随之调整；甚至在看到第十个输出样例时，他们才会想到一些最初根本未曾设想过的失败模式——而这些用户可是经验丰富的专家啊！他们曾构建过多个LLM管道和智能体模型，却仍无法预知所有可能的难点。这种现象在当今AI开发领域尤为典型。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is a really good point. That's very much reinforcing what we were just talking about and that's why I'll pull this up, is just... Okay-
turns.zh: 这一点说得太好了。这正好印证了我们刚刚讨论的内容，所以我要把这段内容调出来供大家参考。好的，继续吧。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: The research behind it.
turns.zh: 背后的研究工作。

I know, obviously, depends complexity to the product, but what's a number in your experience?
turns.zh: 是啊，好的，太棒了。你还是得按老方法做产品，但现在有了一个非常强大的工具，能帮你确保开发出来的东西是正确的。它并不会取代PRD流程。不错。通常你们会用多少个，比如，我不知道，用LLM作为评判者的提示语呢？我不知道。显然这取决于产品的复杂程度，但根据你的经验，平均有多少个提示语呢？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: For me, between four and seven.
turns.zh: 对我来说，时间在四点到七点之间。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's it.
turns.zh: 就这样了。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: It's not that many, because a lot of the failure modes, as Hamel said earlier, can be fixed by just fixing your prompt. You just didn't think to put it in your prompts, so now you put it in your... You shouldn't do an eval like this for everything, just the pesky ones that you've described your ideal behavior in your agent prompt, but it's still failing.
turns.zh: 这种情况并不多见，因为正如哈梅尔之前所说，许多失败模式都可以通过调整提示语来解决。只是你之前没有想到在提示语中加入这些内容，所以现在你需要将其添加进来……你不必对所有情况都进行这样的评估，只需针对那些在智能体提示语中描述了理想行为却仍未能成功的棘手案例即可。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. Say you found a problem, you fixed it. In traditional software development, you'd write a unit test to make sure it doesn't happen again. Is your insight here is, "Don't even bother writing an eval around that if it's just gone"?
turns.zh: 明白了。假设你发现了一个问题并解决了它。在传统软件开发中，你会编写一个单元测试来确保问题不会再次出现。那么你的见解是，如果问题已经消失了，就没必要再为此编写评估代码了吗？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I think you can if you want to, but the whole game here is about prioritizing. You have finite resources and finite time, you can't write an eval for everything, so prioritize the ones that are the more pesky areas.
turns.zh: 我觉得如果你愿意的话是可以做到的，但关键在于要学会取舍。你的资源和时间都是有限的，不可能为所有问题都写评估报告，所以应该优先处理那些最棘手的领域。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Probably the ones that are most risky to your business if they say something like Mecha Hitler, Grok.
turns.zh: 要是他们说出“机械希特勒”、“格罗克”之类的名字，那很可能是对你的业务构成最大威胁的。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yikes.
turns.zh: 天哪，真是要命！

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. Okay, so that's very relieving, because this prompt was a lot of work to really think through all these details.
turns.zh: 太好了。好吧，这样就让我松了一口气，因为要仔细考虑所有这些细节，这个提示可真是费了不少功夫。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: But it's a lot of one-time cost. Right now, forever, you can run this on your application.
turns.zh: 但这需要一次性投入大量成本。目前及未来，您都可以在自己的应用程序中运行这个功能。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Okay, data analysis is super powerful, is going to drive lots of improvements very quickly to your application. We showed the most basic kind of data analysis, which is counting, which is accessible to everyone. You can get more sophisticated with the data analysis. There's lots of different ways to sample, look at data. We made it look easy in a sense, but there's a lot of skills here to do to it well. Building an intuition and a nose for how to sort through this data. For example, let's say I find conversational issues, this conversational flow issues. Maybe if I was trying to chase down this problem further, I would think about ways to find other conversational flow issues that I didn't code. I would maybe dig through the data in several ways, and there's different ways to go about this. It's very similar, if not almost exactly similar as traditional analytics techniques that you would do on any product.
turns.zh: 好的，数据分析的功能非常强大，它能迅速为你的应用带来诸多改进。我们展示了最基础的数据分析方式——计数，这对每个人来说都易于上手。当然，你还可以进行更复杂的数据分析，有多种采样和数据查看的方式。我们把它说得简单易懂，但要做好这项工作需要深厚的专业技能。要培养敏锐的直觉，学会如何筛选这些数据。举个例子，假设我发现了对话流程方面的问题。若想进一步追踪这个问题，我可能会思考如何找出未被编码的其他对话流程问题。为此，我可能会从多个角度深入分析数据，而实现这一目标的方法不胜枚举。这与你针对任何产品所采用的传统分析技术非常相似，甚至可以说几乎完全一致。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Give us just a quick sense of what comes next and then let's talk about the debate around evals and a couple more things.
turns.zh: 先简单说一下接下来要讲的内容，然后我们再来探讨一下关于评估的争议以及其他几个问题。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: What comes next after you've built your LLM judge? Well, we find that people just try to use that everywhere they can, so they'll put the LLM judge in unit tests and they will build, "Here are some example traces where we saw that failure, because we labeled it. Now we're going to make those part of unit tests and make sure that, every time we push a change to our code, these tests are going to pass." They also use it for online monitoring. People are making dashboards on this, and I think that's incredible. I think the products that are doing this, they have a very sharp sense of how well their application is performing, and people don't talk about it, because this is their moat. People are not going to go and share all of these things, because it makes sense. If you are an email-writing assistant, and you're doing this and you're doing it well, you don't want somebody else to go and build an email-writing assistant and then get you out of business. (01:08:41): I really want to stress the point that it's try to use these artifacts that you're building wherever possible online, repeatedly use them to drive improvements to your product. Oftentimes, Hamel and I will tell people how to do this up to this very point, and it clicks for people and then they never come back again. Either they have, I don't know, quit their jobs, they're not doing AI development anymore, or they know what to do from here on out. I think it's the latter, but I think it's very powerful.
turns.zh:
在构建完LLM评分器之后，接下来该做什么？我们发现很多人会尽可能地将其应用于各个场景：比如将LLM评分器集成到单元测试中，然后整理一些示例追踪记录（这些记录来自我们标注过的失败案例），确保每次代码提交时这些测试都能通过。此外，人们还将其用于在线监控，开发相关的仪表盘系统。我认为这非常了不起。那些成功应用该技术的公司，能清晰洞察应用的运行状态，但往往不轻易透露这些信息，因为这构成了他们的核心竞争力。毕竟，如果你开发的是邮件写作助手，而你的竞争对手借助同样的技术反超，那就得不偿失了。

（01:08:41）我特别想强调一点：要尽可能将你开发的这些工具应用于线上场景，持续利用它们来推动产品迭代。很多时候，我和哈梅尔会把这个思路详细讲解给听众，他们听完后豁然开朗，从此踏上正轨。要么他们辞职离开AI开发领域，要么彻底掌握了后续的优化方向。我更倾向于后者，但无论如何，这种方法都极具实战价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just watching you do this really opened my eyes to what this is and how systematic the process is. I always imagine you just sit on a computer, "Okay, what are the things I need to make sure work correctly?" What you're showing us here is it's a very simple step-by-step based on real things that are happening in your product, how to catch them, identify them, prioritize them, and then catch them if they happen again and fix them.
turns.zh: 光是看你做这件事，就让我深刻认识到这项工作的本质，以及整个流程是多么系统化。我一直以为你只需要坐在电脑前，问自己：“哪些功能需要确保正常运行？”但你今天展示的，是基于产品实际情况的分步骤操作——如何发现问题、识别问题、优先处理问题，以及在问题再次出现时及时修复。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, it's not magic. Anyone can do this, you're going to have to practice the skill, like any new skill, you have to practice, but you can do it. I think what's very empowering now is that product managers are doing this and can do this, and can really build very, very profitable products with this skill set.
turns.zh: 是啊，这可不是魔法。任何人都能做到这一点，就像学习任何新技能一样，你得反复练习。但只要下定决心，就一定能成功。我觉得现在最振奋人心的是，产品经理们正在掌握并应用这种技能，他们能够凭借这套技能打造出极具盈利能力的产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, great segue to a debate that we got pulled into that was happening on X the other day. I did not realize how much controversy and drama there is around evals. There's a lot of people with very strong opinions. How about Shreya? Give us just a sense of the two sides of the debate around the importance and value of evals, and then give us your perspective.
turns.zh: 好的，接下来我们来聊聊前几天在X平台上引发的热议。我之前完全没意识到关于评估（evals）的争议和戏剧性场面竟如此激烈。参与讨论的人各执己见，态度十分坚决。施瑞亚（Shreya），你能否先为我们概括一下关于评估重要性和价值的辩论双方观点，再谈谈你个人的看法？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah. All right, I'll be a little bit placating and I say I think everyone is on the same side. I think the misconception is that people have very rigid definitions of what evals is. For example, they might think that evals is just unit tests or they might think that evals is just the data analysis part and no online monitoring or no monitoring of product-specific metrics, like actually number of chats engaged in or whatnot. I think everyone has a different mindset of evals going in, and the other thing I will say is that people have been burned by evals in the past. I think people have done evals badly. One concrete example of this is they've tried to do an LLM judge, but it has not aligned with their expectations. They only uncovered this later on and then they didn't trust it anymore, and then they're like, "I'm anti evals." (01:11:14): I 100% empathize with that, because you should be anti Likert scale LLM judge. I absolutely agree with you, we are anti that as well. A lot of the misconception stems from two things, like people having a narrow definition of evals and then people not doing it well and then getting burned and then wanting to avoid other people making that mistake. Then, unfortunately, X or Twitter is a medium where people are misinterpreting what everybody is saying all the time, and you just get all these strong opinions of, "Don't do evals, it's bad. We tried it, it doesn't work. We're Claude Code," or whatever other famous product, "And we don't do evals." There's just so much nuance behind all of it, because a lot of these applications are standing on the shoulders of evals. Coding agents is a great example of that, Claude Code. They're standing on the shoulders of Claude base model... Not base, but the fine-tuned Claude models have been evaluated on many coding benchmarks. Can't argue against that.
turns.zh: 是啊，好吧，我稍微缓和一下语气，我觉得大家其实都站在同一立场。我认为误区在于人们对评估的定义过于僵化。比如，他们可能认为评估就只是单元测试，或者只包括数据分析环节，而忽略了在线监测或产品特定指标的追踪，比如实际参与的聊天次数之类的。我觉得每个人对评估的理解都存在偏差。另外，我要说的是，过去人们在评估方面吃过亏。比如，他们曾尝试进行LLM评测，但结果与预期不符。直到后来才发现问题所在，进而失去信任，进而变得反感评估。（01:11:14）我完全理解这种情绪，因为你确实应该反感基于Likert量表的LLM评测。我完全赞同你的观点，咱们也反对这种做法。很多误解源于两个方面：一是人们对评估的定义狭隘；二是评估实施不当导致失败后，人们为了避免重蹈覆辙而形成刻板印象。可惜的是，X或Twitter这样的平台上，人们总是在曲解他人的观点。于是就出现了各种极端言论，比如"别做评估，太糟糕了""我们试过，不行""我们用Claude Code"，或者引用其他知名产品案例"我们从不做评估"。这些言论背后其实有很多微妙之处，因为许多应用都是站在评估的肩膀上发展起来的。比如编程代理Claude Code，它就是基于Claude基础模型的改进版本...不准确说，应该说Claude的微调模型在多个编程基准测试中都表现出色。这点无可厚非。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just to make clear exactly what you're talking about there, one of the heads, I think maybe the head engineer of Claude Code, went on a podcast and he's like, "We don't do evals, we just vibe. We just look at vibes," and vibes meaning they just use it and feel if it's right or wrong.
turns.zh: 先说清楚你具体在说什么。Claude Code公司的某位高管（可能是首席工程师）在播客上表示：“我们不做评估，我们只追求直觉。我们就是观察用户的反应，”这里的“直觉”指的是他们在使用产品时，凭感觉判断其是否合适。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I think that works. There's two things to that, right? One is they're standing on the shoulders of the evals that their colleagues are doing for coding.
turns.zh: 我觉得这个办法可行。关键在于两个点，对吧？首先，他们是借助同事们在编码方面所做的评估工作来提升自己的能力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Of the Claude foundational model.
turns.zh: 关于克劳德基础模型的内容。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Absolutely, right? We know that they report those numbers, because we see the benchmarks, we know who's doing well on those. The other thing is they are actually probably very systematic about the error analysis to some extent. I bet you that they're monitoring who is using Claude, how many people are using Claude, how many traps are being created, how long these chats are. They're also probably monitoring in their internal team, they're dogfooding. Anytime something is off, they maybe have a cue or they send it to the person developing Claude Code, and this person is implicitly doing some form of hair error analysis that Hamel talked about. All of this is evals, right? There's no world in which they're just being like, "I made Claude Code, I'm never looking at anything," and unfortunately, when you don't think about that or talk about that, I think that the community... (01:13:39): Most of the community is beginners or people who don't know about evals and want to learn about it, and it sends the wrong message there. Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
turns.zh: 绝对没错，对吧？我们知道他们会上报这些数据，因为我们能看到基准测试结果，也知道哪些用户表现出色。另外，他们很可能在一定程度上对错误分析进行了系统化管理。我敢打赌，他们正在监控谁在使用Claude、使用Claude的用户数量、生成的对话陷阱数量以及对话时长。他们内部团队可能也在进行自测，每当出现异常情况时，他们或许会收到警示，或者将问题反馈给Claude Code的开发团队，而后者正在进行哈梅尔所提及的隐性错误分析。这一切都是评估工作，对吧？绝不可能出现他们只是说“我开发了Claude Code，从不查看任何数据”的情况。但遗憾的是，当人们忽视或回避谈论这些问题时，我认为整个社区……（01:13:39）：社区中大多数是新手，或者是对评估一无所知却想学习的人，这会传递出错误的信息。当然，我不了解Claude Code的具体做法，但我敢打赌，他们肯定在进行某种形式的评估工作。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: We'll also say that coding agents are fundamentally very different than other AI products, because the developer is the domain expert, so you can short circuit a lot of things, and also, the developer is using it all day long, so there's a type of dogfooding and type of domain expertise that is... You can collapse the activities, you don't need as much data, you don't need as much feedback or exploration, because you know, so your eval process should look different.
turns.zh: 我们还要指出，编码代理与其他人工智能产品有着根本的不同。这是因为开发者本身就是领域专家，所以很多问题可以通过捷径解决。此外，开发者会全天使用这些工具，因此存在一种“自家产品测试”（dogfooding）现象，以及深厚的领域专业知识……你可以简化开发流程，不需要收集过多数据，也无需进行大量反馈或探索，因为开发者对系统已然了如指掌。因此，评估流程也应与之相适应。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Because you're seeing the code, you see the code it's generating. You can tell, "This is great, this is terrible."
turns.zh: 既然你能看到代码，就能看到它生成的结果。你可以评价道："这太棒了，这太糟糕了。"

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah, yeah. I think a lot of people had generalized coding agents, because coding agents are the first AI product released into the wild, and I think it's a mistake to try to generalize that at large.
turns.zh: 是啊，是啊。我觉得很多人都把编码代理想得太复杂了，毕竟编码代理是首个真正面向大众推出的AI产品。但我认为把它神化成万能工具是错误的。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: The other thing is, yeah, engineers have a dogfooding personality. There are plenty of applications where people are trying to build AI in certain domains and they don't have dogfooding for doctors, for example, or not out there trying to get all the most incorrect advice from AI and be tolerant and receptive to that. It's very important to keep, I think these nuanced things in mind.
turns.zh: 另外一件事是，没错，工程师们确实有自测的心态。很多应用场景下，人们试图在特定领域开发人工智能技术，但却没有为医生等群体提供自测功能。例如，人们不会去尝试获取人工智能给出的最不准确的建议，也不会对此持宽容和包容的态度。我认为，在处理这些微妙的问题时，保持清醒的认知至关重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What I'm hearing from you, Shreya, interestingly, is that if humans on the team are doing very close data analysis, error analysis, dogfooding like crazy, and essentially, they're the human evals and you're describing that as that's within the umbrella of evals. You could do it that way if you have time and motivation to do that, or you could set these things up to be automatic.
turns.zh: 谢瑞亚，我从你这里听到的很有意思的一点是，如果团队中的人类成员正在进行非常细致的数据分析、错误分析、疯狂的自我测试（dogfooding）等工作——本质上，他们就是人类评估者，而你把这类工作归入评估范畴。如果你有时间和意愿去做这些事，当然可以采用这种方法；但你也可以把这些流程自动化起来。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Absolutely, it's also about the skills. People who work at Anthropic are very, very highly skilled. They've been trained in data analysis or software engineering or AI, and whatnot. You can get there, anyone can get there, of course, by learning the concepts, but most people don't have that skill right now.
turns.zh: 确实，这也关乎技能。Anthropic的员工都非常、非常高技能。他们接受过数据分析、软件工程或人工智能等领域的专业训练。当然，只要掌握了相关概念，任何人都能达到这样的水平，但目前大多数人并不具备这些技能。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Dogfooding is a dangerous one, only because a lot of people will say they're dogfooding. They're like, "Yeah, we dogfooded," but are they, really? A lot of people aren't really dogfooding it at that visceral level that you would need to close that feedback loop. That's the only caveat I would add.
turns.zh: 内部测试产品（dogfooding）这件事挺危险的，主要是因为很多人都会声称自己在进行内部测试。他们会说：“是啊，我们内部测试过了。”但他们真的做到位了吗？很多人的内部测试并没有达到那种真正深入、能有效闭合反馈循环的程度。这是我唯一要补充的警示之言。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's also this, feels like, straw man argument of evals versus A-B tests. Talk about your thoughts there, because that feels like a big part of this debate. People are having like, "Do you need evals if you have A-B tests that are testing production level metrics?"
turns.zh: 还有这样一个似是而非的论点，即评估与A/B测试相对立。能否谈谈你对此的看法？因为这似乎是这场争论的核心所在。人们会问："如果你已经在进行测试生产级别的指标的A/B测试了，那还需要额外的评估吗？"

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: A-B tests are, again, another form of evals ,I imagine, right? When you're doing an A-B test, you have two different experimental conditions and then you have a metric that quantifies the success of something, and you're comparing the metric. Again, an eval in our mind is systematic measurement of quality, some metric. You can't really do an A-B test without the eval to compare, so maybe we just have a different weird take on it.
turns.zh: 又说回A/B测试，我想这也是评估的一种形式吧？在做A/B测试时，会设置两种不同的实验条件，然后用某个指标来衡量某项事物的成功与否，再对这两个指标进行对比。说到评估，在我们看来就是对质量的系统性衡量，某种量化指标。如果没有可以对比的评估标准，A/B测试其实就无从谈起。所以或许我们对这两者的理解存在偏差。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, okay. What I'm hearing is you consider A-B tests as part of the suite of evals that you do. I think when people think A-B tests, it's like we're changing something in the product, we're going to see if this improves some metric we care about. Is that enough? Why do we need to test every little feature? If it's impacting a metric we care about as a business, we have a bunch of A-B tests that are just constantly running.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。我的理解是，你们把A/B测试视为评估套件的一部分。我觉得当人们想到A/B测试时，通常会认为这是对产品进行某种改进，然后观察这些改动是否能提升某个关键指标。这样就足够了吗？为什么我们要对每个微小的功能都进行测试呢？如果某个功能会影响我们业务关心的核心指标，那我们就会安排一堆A/B测试，不断地进行测试验证。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: This is now a great point. I think a lot of people prematurely do A-B tests, because they've never done any error analysis in the first place. They just have hypothetically come up with their product requirements and they believe that, "We should test these things," but it turns out, when you get into the data, as Hamel showed, that the errors that you're seeing are not what you thought what the errors might be. They were these weird handoff issues or, I don't know, the text message thing was strange. I would say that, if you're going to do A-B tests and they're powered by actual error analysis as we've shown today, then that's great, go do it. But if you're just going to do them, which we find that people try to do, just want to do them based on what you hypothetically think is what is important, then I would encourage people to go and rethink that and ground your hypotheses.
turns.zh: 这一点现在很重要。我认为很多人过早地进行A/B测试，是因为他们从未进行过任何错误分析。他们只是凭空构想出产品需求，然后就觉得"我们应该测试这些功能"，但结果是，当你深入研究数据时，正如哈梅尔所展示的，你所发现的错误并非你想象中的那些。可能是一些奇怪的交接问题，又或者短信功能出了故障。我想说，如果你要进行A/B测试，并且像我们今天展示的那样，基于实际的错误分析来开展测试，那当然很棒，尽管去做。但如果你只是想凭空猜测哪些功能重要就急着上手测试，那我建议大家重新审视这个问题，确保你的假设有充分的依据。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have thoughts on what Statsig is going to do at OpenAI? Is there anything there that's interesting? That was a big deal, a huge acquisition. A- B test company people are like, "A-B test, the future." Thoughts?
turns.zh: 关于Statsig即将在OpenAI开展的业务，你有什么看法吗？那里有没有什么值得关注的亮点？这次收购可是件大事啊，业界对此反响热烈。A/B测试领域的从业者都称赞它是"A/B测试的未来"。大家有什么想法吗？

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Just to add to the previous question a little bit, why is there this debate, A-B testing versus evals? I think, fundamentally, evals is... People are trying to wrap their head around how to improve their applications and fundamentally need to do... Data science is useful in products. Looking at data, doing data analytics. There's many different suite of tools, and you don't need to invent anything new. Sure, you don't need necessarily the whole breadth of data science, and it looks slightly different, just slightly, with LLMs. Your tactics might be different, so really what it is is using analytic tools to understand your product. Now, people say the word "Evals," trying to carve out this new thing, and saying evals and then A-B testing, but if you zoom out, it's the same data science as before, and I think that's what's causing the confusion is, "Hey, we need data science thinking," and AI product is helpful to have that thinking in AI products like it is in any product is my take on that.
turns.zh: 补充一下之前的问题：为什么会出现A/B测试与评估（Evals）之争？我认为根本上，评估（Evals）是……人们试图理解如何改进应用程序，而这根本上需要……数据科学在产品中是很有用的。研究数据、进行数据分析。现在有很多不同的工具套件，你无需重新发明轮子。当然，你不一定需要数据科学的全部内容，而在LLM（大语言模型）时代，应用场景略有不同。你的策略可能会有所调整，但本质上还是在用分析工具来理解你的产品。现在人们提起“Evals”，试图开创新概念，把评估和A/B测试分开，但退一步来看，这和过去的数据科学本质上是一回事。我认为造成混淆的原因在于，“嘿，我们需要数据科学思维”，而人工智能产品和其他产品一样，都能从这种思维中受益——这就是我的看法。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's a really good take, I think just the word "Evals" triggers people now.
turns.zh: 这一观点真是太有道理了。我觉得现在一提到“评估”这个词，人们就会立刻产生警惕心理。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If you just call it, "We're just doing error analysis, doing data science to understand where our product breaks and just setting up tests to make sure we know-"
turns.zh: 如果你只是说"我们只是在做错误分析，利用数据科学来了解产品哪里出了问题，然后设置测试来确保我们能掌握情况"——

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: That's boring, sounds boring. No, no, no. We need a mysterious term, like "Evals," to really get the momentum going. Your question about Statsig, I think it's very exciting. To be honest, I don't know much about it, because I just imagine that they're this company that... There's a tool that many people use, and maybe it just so happened that OpenAI acquired them. I'm sure they've been using them in the past, I'm sure OpenAI's competitors are using Statsig as well, so maybe there is something strategic in that acquisition. I have no idea, I don't know anything there, but I think those are really the bigger questions for me than, "Is this fundamentally changing A-B testing or making evals more of a priority?" I think they've always been a priority, I think OpenAI has always been doing some form of them, and OpenAI has gone so far, historically speaking, as to go and look at all the Twitter sentiment and try to do some retrospective on that, and then tie that back to their products. Certainly, they're doing-
turns.zh:
太无聊了，听起来很无聊。不不不。我们需要一个神秘的术语，比如"Evals"，才能真正激发讨论热情。关于Statsig的问题，我觉得这非常令人兴奋。说实话，我对它了解不多，因为我只是觉得他们是一家...  
（此处原文有缺失，可能是对话未完整记录）

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Then, tie that back to their products. Certainly, they're doing some amount of evals before they ship their new foundation models, but they're going so much beyond and being like, "Okay, let's find all the tweets that are complaining about it, all the Reddit threads that are complaining about it, and go try to figure out what's going on." It goes to show that evals are very, very important. No one has really figured it out yet. People are using all the available sources signal that they can to improve their products.
turns.zh: 然后，将这一点与他们的产品联系起来。当然，他们在推出新款粉底产品前会进行一定程度的评估，但他们的做法远不止于此。他们会主动去寻找所有抱怨相关问题的推特帖子和Reddit论坛话题，深入分析问题根源。这充分说明了用户评价的重要性。目前还没有人能完全掌握其中的奥秘，但各大品牌正在充分利用一切可用的信息反馈来改进产品。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: What I'll say is I'm really hopeful that it might shift or create a focus within OpenAI, hopefully. Up until now, a lot of the big labs understandably focused on general benchmarks like MMLU score, human eval, things like that, which are very important for foundation models. Those not very related to product specific evals, like the ones we talked about today, but handoff and stuff like that, they tend not to correlate.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，我真的希望OpenAI内部能有所转变，或是形成新的工作重点。到目前为止，许多大型实验室都在合理地专注于通用基准测试，比如MMLU得分、人类评估等，这些对于基础模型来说确实非常重要。但像我们今天讨论的这些与产品特定评估关系不大的任务，比如交接工作之类的，往往与这些基准测试并无关联。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, they don't correlate with math problem-solving, sorry to say.
turns.zh: 是啊，它们和数学解题能力毫无关联，说实话挺遗憾的。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Exactly. If you look at the eval products, let's say the ones up until recently that some of the big labs have, they don't have error analysis. They have a suite of generic tools, cosine similarity, hallucination score, whatever, and that doesn't work. It's a good first stab at it. It's okay. At least you're doing something, getting people, maybe it's like getting people look at data. But eventually, what we hope to see is, okay, a bit more data science thinking in this eval process. That's hopefully the tools we'll get to.
turns.zh: 没错。看看那些评估产品，比如最近一些大实验室推出的产品，它们根本没有错误分析功能。它们只是提供了一套通用工具，比如余弦相似度、幻觉得分之类的，但这根本不管用。这种做法算是初步尝试，还算可以。至少你在行动，动员了团队，也许还能让大家关注数据。但最终，我们希望看到的是，在评估过程中能融入更多数据科学的思维方式。希望我们未来能开发出更完善的评估工具。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, Pamela and I should not be the only two people on the planet that are promoting a structured way of thinking about application specific evals. It's mind-boggling to me. Why are we the only two people doing this the whole world? What's wrong? I hope that we're not the only people and that more people catch on.
turns.zh: 是啊，我和帕梅拉不应该成为地球上唯一两个倡导针对特定应用进行结构化评估的人。这真让我感到难以置信。为什么全世界只有我们两个人在做这件事？到底哪里出了问题？我希望我们不是孤军奋战，希望能有更多人意识到这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The fact that your course on Maven is the number one highest grossing course in Maven, clearly there's demand and interest, and there's more people I think on your side. Interestingly, just as an example you've been sharing on Twitter that I think is informative, everyone's been saying how cloud code doesn't care about evals. They're all about vibes, and everyone's like, and they're the best coding agent out there, so clearly, this is right. More recently, there's all this talk about Codex, OpenAI Codex being better and everyone's switching and they're so pro evals.
turns.zh: 你的Maven课程在Maven平台上排名第一，收益最高，这显然说明市场需求旺盛、用户兴趣浓厚。我觉得支持你的人肯定更多。说个有趣的例子，你在推特上分享的信息很有启发性——大家都在说云端编程不看重代码评分（evals），讲究的是开发体验（vibes），还有人说它是市面上最棒的编程助手。这显然印证了你的观点。最近关于Codex的讨论更是热烈，OpenAI的Codex被誉为更出色的编程助手，大家都在转用它，而且对代码评分的重视程度明显提升。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: It gets me every time. The Internet's so inconsistent. My favorite thing was yesterday, I believe, a couple of lab mates and I were out getting dessert or something, and somebody said like, "Oh, do you like Codex or Claude better or whatever?" The other person said, "Oh, I like Claude." Then, someone else said, "But the new version of Codex is better." Then, the first person said, "Oh, but the last I checked was two days ago, so maybe my thoughts, maybe I'm not up-to-date." I was like, "Oh, my God."
turns.zh: 每次都让我无语。互联网真是反复无常。昨天发生的事最让我无奈，我记得当时和几个实验室的伙伴出去吃甜点之类的，有人突然问：“哦，你更喜欢Codex还是Claude啊？”对方回答：“哦，我更喜欢Claude。”接着又有人说：“不过新版的Codex更好用啊。”然后第一个人又说：“但我上次查看还是两天前呢，说不定我的信息已经过时了呢？”我当时简直要气炸了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So true, so true. This is the world we live in. Oh, my God. Okay. I want to ask about just top misconceptions people have with evals and top tips and tricks for being successful. Maybe just share one or two each of each. Let me just start with misconceptions, and maybe I'll go to the Hamel first. Just what are a couple of the most common misconceptions people have with eval still?
turns.zh: 太对了，太对了。这就是我们生活的世界。天哪。好吧。我想问问大家对评估的常见误区，以及取得成功的实用技巧和窍门。或许每种问题各分享一两个。我先从误区说起，然后再谈谈哈梅尔（Hamel）的相关内容。大家对评估还有哪些最常见的误区呢？

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: The top one is, "Hey, I can just buy a tool, plug it in, and it'll do the eval for you. Why do I have to worry about this? We live in the age of AI. Can't the AI just eval it?" That's the most common misconception, and people want that so much that people do sell it, but it doesn't work. That's the first one.
turns.zh: 上面那个误区是：“嘿，我只要买个工具，插上电源，它就能帮我完成评估了。我干嘛还要自己操心这些事？我们都生活在人工智能时代了，难道AI不能直接评估吗？” 这是最常见的误区，人们对此需求极高，以至于有人专门卖这类产品，但效果却不尽如人意。这就是第一个误区。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Shoot, many humans are still great. I think that's great news.
turns.zh: 天哪，许多人类还是很棒的。我觉得这真是个好消息。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: The second one that I see a lot is, "Hey, just not looking at the data." In my consulting, people come to me with problems all the time, and the first thing I'll say is, "Let's go look at your traces." You can see their eyes pop open and be like, "What do you mean?" I'm like, "Yeah, let's look at it right now." They're surprised that I am going to go look at individual traces, and it always 100% of the time learn a lot and figure out what the problem is. I think people just don't know how powerful looking at the data is like we showed on this podcast.
turns.zh: 我经常听到的第二个说法是：“嘿，你根本就没看数据啊。”在我的咨询工作中，人们总是带着问题来找我，而我首先会说：“我们先去看看你的日志吧。”你能看到他们眼睛突然一亮，问：“你这话什么意思？”我会说：“对啊，现在就去看看。”他们惊讶于我居然要逐一查看日志记录，而每次这样做都能让我收获大量信息，最终找出问题的根源。我觉得人们根本不知道查看数据能带来多大的价值——就像我们在播客里展示的那样。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I would agree with that.
turns.zh: 我同意这一观点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Those are the top two? Okay.
turns.zh: 就这两个最棒的？好吧。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything else or those are the ones solve those problems.
turns.zh: 还有其他办法吗？还是说这些就是解决那些问题的唯一方法？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Oh, those are definitely... Then, I guess the third one I would add is, there's no one correct way to do evals. There are many incorrect ways of doing evals, but there are also many correct ways of doing it. You got to think about where you are at with your product, how much resources you have, and figure out the plan that works best for you. It'll always involve some form of error analysis as we showed today, but how you operationalize those metrics is going to change based on where you're at.
turns.zh: 哦，那些肯定是……那么，我想我要补充的第三点是，进行评估并没有一种标准的正确方法。评估方法中有很多错误的做法，但也有许多正确的做法。你需要考虑你的产品所处的阶段、可用资源的多少，并制定最适合自己的方案。正如我们今天展示的，这总会涉及某种形式的错误分析，但如何将这些指标付诸实践，将会因你所处的阶段而有所不同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay. What are a couple of just tips and tricks you want to leave people with as they start on their eval journey or just try to get better at something they're already doing?
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的。当人们刚开始踏上评估之旅，或者只是想在现有工作中有所提升时，你有什么实用的小贴士或技巧可以分享给他们呢？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Tip number one is just don't be alarmed or don't be scared of looking at your data. The process, we try to make it as structured as possible. There are inevitably questions that are going to come up. That's totally fine. You might feel like you're not doing it perfectly. That's also fine. The goal is not to do evals perfectly, it's to actionably improve your product. We guarantee you, no matter what you do, if you're doing parts of these process, you're going to find ways of actionable improvement, and then you're going to iterate on your own process from there. (01:27:14): The other tip that I would say is, we are very pro-AI. Use LLMs to help you organize any thoughts that you have throughout this entire process. This could be everything ranging from initial product requirements. Figure out how to organize them for yourself. Figure out how to improve on that product requirements doc based on the open codes that you've created. Don't be afraid to use AI in ways that present information better for you.
turns.zh: 首要建议是，别对查看数据感到惊慌或恐惧。我们会尽可能让整个流程结构化，但难免会遇到各种问题。没关系！你可能会觉得自己做得不够完美，这也很正常。评估的关键不在于追求完美，而是要切实提升产品质量。我们保证，无论你处于流程的哪个阶段，只要你践行了部分步骤，就能找到可行的改进方向，并在此基础上不断优化自己的流程。（01:27:14）另外，我想说的是，我们大力支持人工智能的应用。利用大语言模型来整理整个流程中的思路吧——从最初的产品需求，到根据已创建的开放代码优化需求文档，再到用更易理解的形式呈现这些需求。别犹豫，勇敢地利用AI技术，让信息呈现方式更符合你的需求。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Sweet, so don't be scared. Use LLMs as much as you can throughout the process.
turns.zh: 太棒了，所以别担心。整个过程中，尽可能多地利用大语言模型（LLM）吧。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: But not to replace yourself.
turns.zh: 但不是为了取代你自己。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Right. Okay, great. There's still jobs. It's great. Hamel.
turns.zh: 好的，没错。嗯，太好了。还是有工作机会的，这真是太棒了。哈梅尔。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Yeah. Let me actually share my screen, because I want to show something. To piggyback of what Shreya said is, if you heard any phrase in this podcast, you've probably heard look at your data more than anything else. It's so important that we teach that you should create your own tools to make it as easy as possible. I showed you some tools when we're going through the live example of how to annotate data. Most of the people I work with, they realize how important this is and they vibe code their own tools, or we shouldn't say vibe code. They make their own tools, and it's cheaper than ever before because you have AI that can help you. (01:28:40): AI is really good at creating simple web applications that can show you data, that can write to a database. It's very simple. For the Nurture Boss use case, we wanted to remove all the friction of looking at data. What you see here is just some screenshots of what the application that they created looks like. It's just, "Okay, they have the different channels, voice, email, text. They have the different threads, they hid the system prompt by default." Little quality of life improvements. Then, they actually have this axial coding part here where you can see in red the count of different errors. They automated that part in a nice way and they created this within a few hours. It's really hard to have a one size fits all thing for looking at your data. You don't have to go here immediately, but something to think about is make it as easy as possible because, again, it's the most powerful activity that you can engage in. It's the highest ROI activity you can engage in. With AI, yeah, just remove all the friction.
turns.zh: 是的。让我实际分享一下我的屏幕吧，因为我想展示一些东西。正如Shreya所说，如果你在本期播客中听到了任何一句建议，那很可能是"最重要的是看数据"。我们强调要自建工具来尽可能简化这一流程，这一点至关重要。我在演示如何实时标注数据的例子时，向大家展示了一些工具。大多数与我合作的人都意识到这一点的重要性，他们要么自己编写代码（不过不该用"编写代码"这种口语化表达），总之就是开发自己的工具。如今借助AI技术，创建能展示数据、能与数据库交互的简单网络应用比以往任何时候都更容易。（01:28:40）AI特别擅长创建能展示数据的简单应用，比如显示数据、写入数据库等功能。整个过程非常简单。以Nurture Boss这个案例为例，我们希望消除查看数据时的所有阻碍。你们看到的这些截图展示了他们开发的应用界面：不同的沟通渠道（语音、邮件、短信），隐藏默认的系统提示等，这些都是提升用户体验的细节。最重要的是，他们还开发了这个轴心编码模块，红色标注的不同错误数量一目了然。他们用智能化方式自动化了这一流程，仅用几个小时就完成了开发。查看数据这件事很难有一刀切的解决方案。大家不必急于照搬，但需要思考如何尽可能简化流程，毕竟这才是最能提升效率的核心活动，也是回报率最高的行为。借助AI技术，关键在于消除所有阻碍。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's amazing. Again, I think that ROI piece is so important. We haven't even touched on this enough. The goal here is to make your product better, which will make your business more successful. This isn't just a little exercise to catch bugs and things like that. This is the way to make AI products better because the experience is how users interact with your AI.
turns.zh: 太棒了。再说一次，我认为投资回报率这部分非常重要。我们对此甚至还谈得不够。这里的目标是让你的产品更出色，从而让你的业务更加成功。这不只是查找漏洞之类的简单测试。这是提升AI产品质量的关键途径，因为用户与AI的交互体验直接影响着产品的成败。

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: Absolutely. If any, we teach our students, "Hey, when you're doing these evals, if you see something that's wrong, just go fix it." The whole point is not to have evals, a beautiful eval suite, where you can point at it, edit it and say, Oh, look at my evals." No, just fix your application, make it better. If it's obvious, do it. Totally agree with you.
turns.zh: 完全同意。如果有问题的话，我们会教导学生：“嘿，当你在进行这些评估时，如果你发现有任何错误，就直接去修正它。”关键不在于拥有一套漂亮的评估套件，让你可以指着它、编辑它，然后说：“看我的评估多棒啊！”不，你只需要去修复你的应用程序，让它变得更好。只要问题明显，就直接动手改进。完全赞同你的观点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. A question I didn't ask, but this is I think something people are thinking about. How long do you spend on this? How long does it usually take to do? The first time
turns.zh: 太棒了。虽然我没问这个问题，但我觉得这是大家都在思考的。你花了多长时间做这个？通常做一次需要多久？第一次做的时候呢？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: I can answer for myself for applications that I work with. Usually, I'll spend three to four days really working with whoever to do initial rounds of error analysis. A lot of labeling, feel like we're in a good place to create the spreadsheet that Hamel had and everyone's on-board and convinced, and even a few LLM judge evaluators. But this is one-time cost. Once I figured out how to integrate that in unit tests, or I have a script that automatically runs it on samples and I'll create a Cron Job to just do this every week. I would say it's like, I don't know, I find myself probably spending more time looking at data because I'm just data hungry like that. I'm so curious. (01:31:23): I'm like, I've gained so much from this process and it's put me above and beyond in any of my collaborations with folks, so I want to keep doing it, but I don't have to. I would say maybe 30 minutes a week after that.
turns.zh: 就我参与的应用项目而言，我可以为自己负责。通常，我会花三到四天时间与相关人员深入开展初步的错误分析工作。期间需要进行大量标注工作，目前我们已成功创建了哈梅尔提到的电子表格，团队成员都已达成共识，甚至包括几位LLM评分员。但这只是一次性投入。一旦我掌握了如何将其集成到单元测试中，或者开发出能自动在样本上运行该流程的脚本后，便会创建一个定时任务，每周自动执行此操作。我得说，我发现自己可能花费了更多时间研究数据，因为我实在太渴望获取更多信息了。我对此充满好奇。（01:31:23）我觉得自己从这个过程中收获颇丰，它让我的合作效率远超预期，所以我很想继续坚持下去，但其实并非必须如此。之后每周可能只需花费约30分钟即可。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's a week essentially, a week essentially upfront, and then 30 minutes to keep improving on adding to your suite?
turns.zh: 基本上就是一周时间，主要是前期准备阶段，之后每隔30分钟就持续优化和完善你的方案，对吧？

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, it's really not that much time. I think people just get overwhelmed by how much time they spend up front and then thinking that they have to keep doing this all the time.
turns.zh: 是啊，其实时间并不算多。我觉得人们只是被前期投入的大量时间压得喘不过气，然后误以为自己必须一直这样坚持下去。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Is there anything else that you wanted to share or leave listeners with? Anything else you wanted to double down as a point before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 太棒了。在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前，还有什么想和听众分享或留下启发的吗？有没有什么观点值得你再强调一遍的？

turns.speaker: Hamel Husain
turns.en: I would say this process is a lot of fun, actually. It's like, okay, you're looking at data. Oh, it sounds like you're annotating things. Okay. Actually, I was just looking at a client's data yesterday, the same exact process. It's a application that sends emails, recruiting emails to try to get candidates to apply for a job. We decided to start looking at traces. We jumped right into it. "Hey, let's look at your traces." We looked at a trace, the first thing I saw was this email that is worded, "Given your background, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah." I asked the person right away, and this is where putting your product hat on and just being critical, and this is where the fun part is. (01:32:55): I said, "You know what? I hate this email. Do you like the email, given your background?" When I receive a message given your background, comma, I just delete that. I'm like, "What is this, given your background with machine learning and blah blah?" I'm like, "This is a generic thing." I asked the person like, "Hey, can we do better than this? This sounds like generic recruiting." They're like, "Oh, yeah, maybe." Because they were proud of it, they're like, "The AI is doing the right thing, it's sending this email with the right information, with the right link, with the right name, everything." That's where the fun part is, is put your product hat on and get into, is this really good?
turns.zh: 实际上，我觉得这个过程挺有趣的。比如，你在看数据，哦，听起来你在标注信息。好吧。我昨天刚看了一个客户的数据，流程完全一样。这是一个发送招聘邮件的应用程序，目的是吸引候选人申请工作。我们决定开始分析追踪数据，直接开干了。"嘿，咱们看看你的追踪数据吧。"我们查看了一条追踪记录，首先映入眼帘的是这封邮件，开头写着"鉴于你的背景，等等等等"。我立刻问对方——这时候你要戴上产品经理的帽子，保持批判性思维，乐趣也从此刻开始。（01:32:55）我说："你知道吗？我讨厌这封邮件。鉴于你的背景，你喜欢这封邮件吗？"我收到这种"鉴于你的背景"的邮件，直接就删掉了。我会想："这算什么？鉴于你有机器学习背景之类的？"我觉得这太普通了。我问对方："嘿，我们能不能做得更好？这听起来就是千篇一律的招聘邮件。"对方回答："哦，或许吧……"他们还挺自豪的，说"人工智能做得很棒，邮件里信息准确，链接正确，名字也合适，一切都完美。"这时候乐趣就来了，戴上产品思维去评判：这真的好吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Something I want to make sure we cover before we get to a very exciting lightning round is, this is just scratching the surface of all the things you need to know to do this well. I think this is the best primer I've ever seen on how to do this well.
turns.zh: 在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前，我想确保我们先把一些基础内容讲清楚。毕竟，要想做好这件事，你需要掌握的知识远不止这些。我觉得这份指南堪称我见过的最佳入门教程，教你如何把这件事做得又好又专业。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Nice.
turns.zh: 不错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: But I think we did it. But you guys teach a course that goes much, much deeper for people that really want to get good at this and take this really seriously. Share what else you teach in the course that we didn't cover, and what else you get as a student being part of the course you teach at Maven.
turns.zh: 但我觉得我们成功了。不过你们开设的课程针对那些真正想精通这门技艺、认真对待它的人，其深度远超我们的课程。请分享一下你们课程中还有哪些内容是我们没有涉及的，以及作为学员参与你们在Maven平台授课的课程能获得哪些额外收获。

turns.speaker: Shreya Shankar
turns.en: Yeah, I can talk about the syllabus a little bit, and then Hamel can talk about all the perks.
